'''Son My I power station''' (Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Sơn Mỹ 1) is a power station in pre-construction in Ham Tan, Bình Thuận, Vietnam.

==Ownership Tree==

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

The Son My I power station received in-principle investment approval from Vietnam's trade ministry in 2021 on the build-operate-transfer (BOT) model, with the start of operations aimed for 2028, as of March 2025.<ref>Tri Duc, [https://theinvestor.vn/central-vietnam-province-to-clear-sites-for-lng-projects-in-may-for-operation-in-2028-d14909.html Central Vietnam province to clear sites for LNG projects in May, for operation in 2028,] The Investor, Mar. 18, 2025</ref> The project cost is estimated to be US$2.2 billion.<ref>Tri Duc, [https://theinvestor.vn/lng-to-power-projects-in-central-vietnam-still-drafting-feasibility-studies-d11294.html LNG-to-power projects in central Vietnam still drafting feasibility studies,] The Investor, Jul. 18, 2024</ref> France's Électricité de France (EDF), Japan’s Sojitz and Kyushu Electric Power, and Vietnam’s Pacific Corporation are project investors.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627175449/https://theinvestor.vn/frances-edf-seeks-to-collaborate-with-vietnams-evn-in-nuclear-power-renewable-energy-d15796.html|title=France's EDF seeks to collaborate with Vietnam's EVN in nuclear power, renewable energy|last=theinvestor.vn|access-date=2025-09-15|language=en}}</ref>
